line: The arrow’s barbed. Lancet first — two nicks at the entry wound.

Burns across the chest, lead driven under the skin — and a note from the Gunsmiths’ Guild pinned to his shirt.
The Guild will pay for his care. Once we have paid the Guild’s fee for inspecting its own burst barrel.

Powder burns. The black crust is dead meat: off with it before any salve, or it festers underneath.

Matthis Kolb, tanner’s man. Written, and underlined.
Buboes, and a rotting sore. He’s slept in the Rows among the hides. Burn the grubs, Kreuzer — not the man.
A plague case. In the city. How very interesting.
…Inquisitor Stroh. Of the Ash Tribunal.

Lance each bubo with a single touch of the Lancet before it bursts.
Then drain the pus and brush Saint’s Salve over it.
Grubs in the sore! The Cautery Brand — hold it on each one until it stops moving.
Don’t linger on bare flesh with the Cautery Brand.
The rot’s spreading. Saint’s Salve on every patch — quickly, it creeps back.
The choir… they’re singing in me… make them stop singing…

The first of the canonical hours. The first prayer of the night.
A curse that lives and fights like a beast, and signs itself like a psalm. A Malison.
And if this was Matins… then somewhere, someone is already writing Lauds.
A remarkable recovery, Doctor. Remarkable.
Tell me — at the end, your hands moved so very quickly. Almost as if time itself were… obliging you.
Practice, Inquisitor. And the grace of Saint Ildra.
Of course. The grace of the Saint. I shall pray on it.
I watched every stroke. No tricks, no prayers. Only a surgeon, working. I find it almost disappointing.
Surgery usually is, Inquisitor. That is how you know it worked.

line: The venom first — hold the Tincture on the bite until it takes.
The longer it spreads, the harder it drags on him.
Now the fangs. Tongs — pull each one clear.
Claw rakes. Three deep lines — drain and stitch each.
Grave-dirt in them too — Leech-Pipe it out before any Saint’s Salve.
Put me down, you long-legged oafs! I can walk! I can… mostly walk.
Dwarf prospector. Her crew was working a seam in the hills when it caved in.
The rock went black, Doctor. Black as a wet eye, and it had a pulse. It sang when we struck it. Then it burst.
Took my lamp with it. So it’s glass in me as well as stone, and you’ll find both.
Mind her beard, Doctor. Every knot in it is tied for a debt.
Nineteen knots. Nine are owed to me, ten I owe. If I die owing ten, my sons pay them, and my sons are idle.
There are shards under her skin I can’t see — but the flesh around them is spoiling.
Master Haller sent his old Scrying Lens with me. He says you are to break anything else of his first.
Dwarf hide’s thicker than yours, lad. You’ll want a strong arm on that thread.
Hold still, Mistress Flintvein, and I’ll owe you a knot.
Rock splinters on the surface first. Tongs.
Now — the Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh; where something hides, it shimmers.
Hold it still over the shimmer to bring the shard to light, then pull it.
Clean up the spoiled flesh and any wounds left.
Elf forager. Checked his snares by the old web-trees yesterday and never came back. We found him at dusk, wrapped like a midwinter ham.
…the brood-mother… she kissed me… she was so gentle about it…
Elf skin, Doctor — thin as vellum. It cuts at a breath and bleeds like a spring.
The foresters call the great web-spinners brood-mothers. Venom, spreading fast. And these lumps… Saints. She laid in him.
My lads won’t fetch water past the web-trees now. They say a brood-mother remembers every face that has seen her.
Then fetch my water from somewhere she hasn’t looked, Captain. And more light.
The sacs are swelling, Doctor. If they hatch on their own, they’ll scatter.
Silk over the bites. Cut each strand with one stroke of the Lancet.
Venom from two bites. Tincture on each, quickly.
The sacs — lance each with one touch, then sear the hatchlings with the Cautery Brand.
Mind the ones that are close to hatching.
Her brood-cluster — three sacs under one skin.
Cut the membrane right around them with the Lancet first, or they’ll wake as one.
One more sac, deeper. Use the Scrying Lens to find it, then open it.
And he’s taken a fever-bubo from the bite — lance and cleanse it.
Doctor. I have brought you a gift.

line: The poison he swallowed — Tincture, now, or he’s gone before we start.
Those sigils are burning him from within. Sear each one out — every stroke.
There — a knot of it round his throat. Every time he hums, it ties itself again.
Burn it out between the verses.
The hexfire burns. Pluck the eschar, then Saint’s Salve on them.
Maggots in an old sore — the Tribunal’s cells are filthy. Cautery Brand.
One more thing — the Scrying Lens. He swallowed something the Tribunal wasn’t to find.
Open him along the line with the Lancet, then the Tongs.
Lauds… is sung at dawn… with the muster… under the banner…
The dawn muster? That’s now—
Who keeps the watch before the sun?
The one who wakes, and wakes alone.
Who sings the day when day is done?
The one we answer, bone to bone.
Doctor! It’s Jorg — there are two of them in his chest, and each one answers the other!
Clear a table. Sister — every instrument we have.
We have to open him — along the line, Doctor.
A choir! Those lights are its Voices — hold the Cautery Brand on each as it circles.
Silence all of them and its heart will be bare.
It’s done. Tend what it left of him.
Close him up. Gently — he has a banner to carry.
And beside it — Doctor, look. An eye with a stroke through it. The same mark the page-boy carried.
Two of them now. Matins in the city, Lauds in my own camp. Someone is keeping time, Doctor.
Six more hours to the full Office. Prime. Terce. Sext. None. Vespers. Compline.
Doctor Kreuzer.
When that thing screamed, every candle in this tent stopped flickering. The flames stood still. For eight heartbeats.
I counted.
…The morning air is very still, Inquisitor.
I watched your hands while that thing screamed. They shook, Doctor. For once.
It was a long night, Inquisitor.
We will speak at length, you and I. After Prime.
Ease off! You’ll tear the joint from its socket.
Pull on the limb first — traction, or the ends grind.
Stop at the end of the line — you’ve nicked him.
Through the skin. Now the layer beneath — trace it again.
There’s a gap in the suture — it’s still bleeding. Close it up.
It keeps filling — stitch the wound beneath it first, then drain.
The pus is getting into that cut — drain it before it festers!
Too much blood — draw it off with the leech-pipe before you stitch!
Salve won’t hold a wound that size. Stitch it first.
It’s whispering to him through the tongs — into the lead dish, quickly!
The hexstone is corrupting the flesh around it — get it out!
It’s in his stomach, Doctor — open him along the line first.
Barbed! Nick the flesh at the entry with the lancet before you pull.
Pull along the line it went in — you’re tearing the channel!
It snapped — the head’s still in there! Ease them out: pull, pause, then draw.
Slowly with glass — it slices as it goes.
Not the tray — hexstone goes in the lead dish!
That one was broken — only the crown came. The root’s still in; tongs again.
A hymn-token — the Choir’s. He swallowed it rather than let the Tribunal find it on him.
Right off the body, Doctor — into the tray, or it sinks back in.
Scraps of wadding went in with the shot — pull those out too, or it’ll fester.
Shot drives wadding in after it. Search with the lens before we close.
It’s festering — the salve sealed the eschar in. Clean that rot.
Green flicker — it’s rekindling! Brand out the ember!
The dead flesh is off. Now salve the raw burn.
The dead core’s out. Pluck the rest of the eschar, then salve.
That centre is dead flesh — cut the char out with the lancet first!
The acid’s still live! Draw it off with the leech-pipe before you salve.
Pluck away the charred eschar with the tongs first!
Its ember still glows — brand it out or the hexfire will rekindle!
Draw a short cut across the crown — a prick won’t open it.
Too long a cut — it’s spilling everywhere. Short and across the crown!
Draw off the pus before you salve it.
The venom’s running for his heart along the vein — sear or draw off the drops, or tie the vein!
One’s burrowed in! Find it with the lens.
Don’t let go half-way — hold the brand until it stops moving!
Don’t stop half-way — the curse heals what you leave!

It’s calling its Voices back!
It heals from the other body! Strike one, then the other — quickly!

The dawn — I can’t see a thing through the Lens! Wait for the glare to pass!
It’s gone under the skin! The Scrying Lens — hunt its ripples!
There! It’s surfacing — brand it before it dives!

Severed! Strike freely while they’re apart!
